title: MD SB114: 3-1-1 Systems - Expansion Program and Oversight Board - Establishment

obligations: The Board shall designate counties to participate in the Program (§ 1-3A-03(A)(1)).
The Board shall establish evaluation criteria for the Program (§ 1-3A-03(A)(2)).
The Board shall review vendor applications submitted by the Maryland Information Network and select a vendor (§ 1-3A-03(A)(3)).
The Board shall ensure 3-1-1 systems align with best practices for technology, accessibility, and equity (§ 1-3A-03(A)(4)).
The Board shall approve and coordinate statewide marketing strategies for the Program (§ 1-3A-03(A)(5)).
The Board shall implement the Program (§ 1-3A-03(A)(6)).
The Board shall establish memorandums of understanding with counties, utilities, and other stakeholders to ensure interoperability (§ 1-3A-03(A)(7)).
The Board shall develop a set of unified statewide data standards for 3-1-1 systems (§ 1-3A-03(A)(8)).
Marketing strategies approved under this section shall be accessible, multilingual, and culturally competent (§ 1-3A-03(B)).
The Board shall establish a 3-1-1 Program (§ 1-3A-04(A)).
The Board shall designate two counties that have 3-1-1 systems and two counties that do not have 3-1-1 systems to participate in the Program (§ 1-3A-04(C)(1)).
The Board shall require the Maryland Information Network to solicit requests for proposals from vendors and submit a list of possible vendors to the Board (§ 1-3A-04(D)).
The Board shall establish a chatbot in each county designated by the Board on or before June 30, 2027 (§ 1-3A-04(E)(1)).

Each chatbot shall include multilingual support, integration with geographic information system data for accurate routing, and clear escalation protocols to route complex requests to live agents (§ 1-3A-04(E)(2)).
Each county participating in the Program shall designate the sources a chatbot may use in responding to questions (§ 1-3A-04(E)(3)(I)).
The vendor of the 3-1-1 system chosen to host a chatbot shall analyze the performance of the chatbot based on user feedback regarding accuracy of chatbot responses (§ 1-3A-04(E)(3)(II)1).
The vendor shall investigate an answer that a user designates as inaccurate (§ 1-3A-04(E)(3)(II)2.A).
If the source is determined to be inaccurate, the agency operating the source webpage shall update it to become accurate (§ 1-3A-04(E)(3)(II)2.B).
The Board shall establish a voicebot in each participating county on or before December 1, 2028 2027 (as written in the text) (§ 1-3A-04(F)(1)).

Each voicebot shall include multilingual support, the ability to transfer calls to 9-1-1, 2-1-1, and 9-8-8, integration with geographic information system data for accurate routing, and clear escalation protocols to route complex requests to live agents (§ 1-3A-04(F)(2)).
The vendor of the 3-1-1 system chosen to host a voicebot shall analyze the performance of the voicebot in the same way as the chatbot under § 1-3A-04(E)(3)(II) (§ 1-3A-04(F)(3)).
The Board shall implement the Program in each county in the State on or before July 1, 2028 according to the implementation plan submitted under § 1-3A-05(B) (§ 1-3A-04(G)).
The Board shall meet at least four times per calendar year (§ 1-3A-02(D)).
The Maryland Information Network shall provide staff to the Board (§ 1-3A-02(G)).

The Board shall submit a progress report to the Governor and General Assembly on or before December 1, 2027 with specified contents including call deflection tracking, subject matter, how calls are addressed, service delivery options, cost estimates, user satisfaction, accessibility, costs saved, evaluation of chatbot and voicebot integration, and recommendations (§ 1-3A-05(A)).

The Board shall submit a report to the Governor and General Assembly on or before July 1, 2028 that evaluates implementation including cost effectiveness, equity, integration challenges, user satisfaction, and 9-1-1 call volume data, and creates a comprehensive implementation plan to expand the Program to each county (§ 1-3A-05(B)).

The 3-1-1 Technical Advisory Committee shall provide technical guidance to the Maryland 3-1-1 Oversight Board and the 3-1-1 Program to avoid negative unintended consequences related to interoperability among Maryland 3-1-1 voicebots and chatbots and existing 3-1-1, 2-1-1, 9-1-1, 9-8-8, and local nonemergency public safety systems (Section 2(d)).
prohibitions: A member of the Board may not receive compensation as a member of the Board (§ 1-3A-02(F)(1)).
A member of the 3-1-1 Technical Advisory Committee may not receive compensation as a member of the Committee (Section 2(c)(1)).
A project site visit or educational field tour may not be considered a meeting of the Board if no organizational business is conducted (§ 1-3A-02(E)).
Nothing in this subtitle shall be construed to require the replacement or preemption of any operations or functions of an existing 3-1-1 system in the State (§ 1-3A-06(1)).
Nothing in this subtitle shall be construed to prohibit a county that has chosen not to participate in the Program from subsequently choosing to participate (§ 1-3A-06(2)).

Passed 2026-05-12. Reading generated by ollama:deepseek-v4-pro from the enrolled text; the full text is at the foot of this page so every statement can be checked against it. LegiScan record · official text

What it does

Establishes the Maryland 3-1-1 Oversight Board within the Maryland Information Network and a 3-1-1 Program to evaluate and expand 3-1-1 systems. Requires the Board to designate counties, select vendors, and deploy AI chatbots and voicebots with multilingual support, GIS integration, and escalation protocols. Requires statewide implementation by July 1, 2028 and reports to the Governor and General Assembly.

Who it applies to

  • Maryland 3-1-1 Oversight Board
  • Maryland Information Network
  • Counties designated to participate in the Program
  • Vendors selected for 3-1-1 technology platforms
  • Agencies operating source webpages used by chatbots and voicebots
  • 3-1-1 Technical Advisory Committee
  • Existing 3-1-1 systems in the State

Effective date

July 1, 2026; Section 2 of the Act (3-1-1 Technical Advisory Committee) remains effective for 2 years and 3 months and is abrogated on September 30, 2028.

Key definitions

  • Artificial intelligence: a machine-based system that: (1) can, for a given set of human-defined objectives, make predictions, recommendations, or decisions influencing real or virtual environments; (2) uses machine and human-based inputs to perceive real and virtual environments and abstracts those perceptions into models through analysis in an automated manner; and (3) uses model inference to formulate options for information or action (§ 3.5-801(c), incorporated by § 1-3A-01(B)).
  • Board: the Maryland 3-1-1 Oversight Board established under § 1-3A-02 (§ 1-3A-01(C)).
  • Chatbot: a computer program available through a phone number, a website, or an application that simulates human conversation through text or voice, using artificial intelligence to respond to typed questions using information from curated, agency-approved sources such as government websites, service catalogs, ordinances, forms, and geographic information system layers (§ 1-3A-01(D)).
  • Program: the 3-1-1 Program established under § 1-3A-04 (§ 1-3A-01(E)).
  • 3-1-1 System: a telephone service or other technology used to access a local government service line, designed for reporting and resolving community infrastructure and service issues on a nonemergency basis (§ 1-3A-01(F)).
  • Voicebot: a computer program available through a phone number that simulates human conversation using artificial intelligence technology that: (1) responds to vocal questions over the phone using information from curated, agency-approved sources such as government websites, service catalogs, ordinances, forms, and geographic information system layers; and (2) routes calls to appropriate destinations (§ 1-3A-01(G)).

Obligations

  • The Board shall designate counties to participate in the Program (§ 1-3A-03(A)(1)).
  • The Board shall establish evaluation criteria for the Program (§ 1-3A-03(A)(2)).
  • The Board shall review vendor applications submitted by the Maryland Information Network and select a vendor (§ 1-3A-03(A)(3)).
  • The Board shall ensure 3-1-1 systems align with best practices for technology, accessibility, and equity (§ 1-3A-03(A)(4)).
  • The Board shall approve and coordinate statewide marketing strategies for the Program (§ 1-3A-03(A)(5)).
  • The Board shall implement the Program (§ 1-3A-03(A)(6)).
  • The Board shall establish memorandums of understanding with counties, utilities, and other stakeholders to ensure interoperability (§ 1-3A-03(A)(7)).
  • The Board shall develop a set of unified statewide data standards for 3-1-1 systems (§ 1-3A-03(A)(8)).
  • Marketing strategies approved under this section shall be accessible, multilingual, and culturally competent (§ 1-3A-03(B)).
  • The Board shall establish a 3-1-1 Program (§ 1-3A-04(A)).
  • The Board shall designate two counties that have 3-1-1 systems and two counties that do not have 3-1-1 systems to participate in the Program (§ 1-3A-04(C)(1)).
  • The Board shall require the Maryland Information Network to solicit requests for proposals from vendors and submit a list of possible vendors to the Board (§ 1-3A-04(D)).
  • The Board shall establish a chatbot in each county designated by the Board on or before June 30, 2027 (§ 1-3A-04(E)(1)).
  • Each chatbot shall include multilingual support, integration with geographic information system data for accurate routing, and clear escalation protocols to route complex requests to live agents (§ 1-3A-04(E)(2)).
  • Each county participating in the Program shall designate the sources a chatbot may use in responding to questions (§ 1-3A-04(E)(3)(I)).
  • The vendor of the 3-1-1 system chosen to host a chatbot shall analyze the performance of the chatbot based on user feedback regarding accuracy of chatbot responses (§ 1-3A-04(E)(3)(II)1).
  • The vendor shall investigate an answer that a user designates as inaccurate (§ 1-3A-04(E)(3)(II)2.A).
  • If the source is determined to be inaccurate, the agency operating the source webpage shall update it to become accurate (§ 1-3A-04(E)(3)(II)2.B).
  • The Board shall establish a voicebot in each participating county on or before December 1, 2028 2027 (as written in the text) (§ 1-3A-04(F)(1)).
  • Each voicebot shall include multilingual support, the ability to transfer calls to 9-1-1, 2-1-1, and 9-8-8, integration with geographic information system data for accurate routing, and clear escalation protocols to route complex requests to live agents (§ 1-3A-04(F)(2)).
  • The vendor of the 3-1-1 system chosen to host a voicebot shall analyze the performance of the voicebot in the same way as the chatbot under § 1-3A-04(E)(3)(II) (§ 1-3A-04(F)(3)).
  • The Board shall implement the Program in each county in the State on or before July 1, 2028 according to the implementation plan submitted under § 1-3A-05(B) (§ 1-3A-04(G)).
  • The Board shall meet at least four times per calendar year (§ 1-3A-02(D)).
  • The Maryland Information Network shall provide staff to the Board (§ 1-3A-02(G)).
  • The Board shall submit a progress report to the Governor and General Assembly on or before December 1, 2027 with specified contents including call deflection tracking, subject matter, how calls are addressed, service delivery options, cost estimates, user satisfaction, accessibility, costs saved, evaluation of chatbot and voicebot integration, and recommendations (§ 1-3A-05(A)).
  • The Board shall submit a report to the Governor and General Assembly on or before July 1, 2028 that evaluates implementation including cost effectiveness, equity, integration challenges, user satisfaction, and 9-1-1 call volume data, and creates a comprehensive implementation plan to expand the Program to each county (§ 1-3A-05(B)).
  • The 3-1-1 Technical Advisory Committee shall provide technical guidance to the Maryland 3-1-1 Oversight Board and the 3-1-1 Program to avoid negative unintended consequences related to interoperability among Maryland 3-1-1 voicebots and chatbots and existing 3-1-1, 2-1-1, 9-1-1, 9-8-8, and local nonemergency public safety systems (Section 2(d)).

Prohibitions

  • A member of the Board may not receive compensation as a member of the Board (§ 1-3A-02(F)(1)).
  • A member of the 3-1-1 Technical Advisory Committee may not receive compensation as a member of the Committee (Section 2(c)(1)).
  • A project site visit or educational field tour may not be considered a meeting of the Board if no organizational business is conducted (§ 1-3A-02(E)).
  • Nothing in this subtitle shall be construed to require the replacement or preemption of any operations or functions of an existing 3-1-1 system in the State (§ 1-3A-06(1)).
  • Nothing in this subtitle shall be construed to prohibit a county that has chosen not to participate in the Program from subsequently choosing to participate (§ 1-3A-06(2)).

Penalties and enforcement

The text does not state any penalties, fines, or private right of action. Enforcement is not specified beyond the Board's duty to implement the Program (§ 1-3A-03(A)(6)) and the Maryland Information Network's duty to provide staff (§ 1-3A-02(G)). No enforcement authority or penalty provisions are provided.

How it affects AI deployment

  • Counties designated for the Program must allow deployment of AI chatbots and voicebots for 3-1-1 services, unless they opt out within 14 days by letter (§ 1-3A-04(C)(2)).
  • AI chatbots must be established in each designated county by June 30, 2027, with multilingual support, GIS integration, and escalation protocols (§ 1-3A-04(E)(1)-(2)).
  • AI voicebots must be established in each participating county by December 1, 2028 2027 (as written), with multilingual support, ability to transfer to 9-1-1, 2-1-1, 9-8-8, GIS integration, and escalation protocols (§ 1-3A-04(F)(1)-(2)).
  • Each participating county must designate the sources its chatbot may use, limiting AI responses to curated, agency-approved sources (§ 1-3A-04(E)(3)(I)).
  • Vendors hosting chatbots and voicebots must analyze performance based on user feedback on accuracy, investigate answers users mark inaccurate, and if a source is inaccurate, the agency operating that source webpage must update it (§ 1-3A-04(E)(3)(II), § 1-3A-04(F)(3)).
  • Statewide implementation in every county is required by July 1, 2028, meaning all counties will eventually have AI 3-1-1 systems unless they determine scope and manner after the July 1, 2028 report (§ 1-3A-04(G), § 1-3A-05(C)).
  • The Board must ensure systems align with best practices for technology, accessibility, and equity, and marketing must be accessible, multilingual, and culturally competent (§ 1-3A-03(A)(4), § 1-3A-03(B)).
  • Technical Advisory Committee guidance aims to avoid negative unintended consequences related to interoperability with existing 9-1-1, 2-1-1, 9-8-8, and local nonemergency systems (Section 2(d)).

Notable exemptions

  • A county designated under § 1-3A-04(C)(1) may choose not to participate by submitting a letter to the Board within 14 days after designation stating the reason (§ 1-3A-04(C)(2)).
  • After the Board submits the report required under § 1-3A-05(B), each county may determine the scope and manner of its participation in the Program (§ 1-3A-05(C)).
  • Nothing in the subtitle requires replacement or preemption of any operations or functions of an existing 3-1-1 system (§ 1-3A-06(1)).
  • A county that chose not to participate may subsequently choose to participate (§ 1-3A-06(2)).
  • A project site visit or educational field tour is not considered a meeting of the Board if no organizational business is conducted (§ 1-3A-02(E)).
  • Board members and Committee members are not compensated but may be reimbursed for expenses under standard State travel regulations (§ 1-3A-02(F), Section 2(c)).

Compliance steps

  • If designated, decide whether to opt out within 14 days by submitting a letter to the Board stating the reason (§ 1-3A-04(C)(2)).
  • If participating, designate the sources the chatbot may use in responding to questions (§ 1-3A-04(E)(3)(I)).
  • Ensure a chatbot is established by June 30, 2027 with multilingual support, GIS integration, and clear escalation protocols (§ 1-3A-04(E)(1)-(2)).
  • Ensure a voicebot is established by December 1, 2028 2027 (as written) with multilingual support, ability to transfer to 9-1-1, 2-1-1, 9-8-8, GIS integration, and escalation protocols (§ 1-3A-04(F)(1)-(2)).
  • If a vendor, analyze chatbot and voicebot performance based on user feedback on accuracy, investigate answers users mark inaccurate, and if a source is inaccurate, ensure the agency updates the source webpage (§ 1-3A-04(E)(3)(II), § 1-3A-04(F)(3)).
  • If an agency operating a source webpage, update inaccurate sources to become accurate (§ 1-3A-04(E)(3)(II)2.B).
  • Participate in the Board's memorandums of understanding and unified statewide data standards (§ 1-3A-03(A)(7)-(8)).
  • Comply with statewide implementation by July 1, 2028 according to the implementation plan submitted under § 1-3A-05(B) (§ 1-3A-04(G)).
  • After the July 1, 2028 report, determine the scope and manner of participation in the Program (§ 1-3A-05(C)).

WES MOORE, Governor Ch. 434

Chapter 434

 (Senate Bill 114)

AN ACT concerning

 3–1–1 Systems – Expansion Program and Oversight Board – Establishment

FOR the purpose of establishing the Maryland 3–1–1 Oversight Board in the Maryland
 Information Network; establishing the 3–1–1 Program to use certain artificial
 intelligence to answer certain questions and route certain calls in certain counties;
 requiring the expansion of creation and implementation of a plan to expand the
 3–1–1 Program to all of the counties in Maryland on or before a certain date;
 establishing the 3–1–1 Technical Advisory Committee; and generally relating to
 3–1–1 systems.

 Article – Public Safety
 Section 1–3A–01 through 1–3A–05 1–3A–06 to be under the new subtitle “Subtitle
 3A. 3–1–1 Nonemergency Community Information and Referral Systems”

 (2022 Replacement Volume and 2025 Supplement)

 Article – State Finance and Procurement
 Section 3.5–801(a) and (c)

 (a) In this subtitle the following words have the meanings indicated.

 (c) “Artificial intelligence” means a machine–based system that:

 (1) can, for a given set of human–defined objectives, make predictions,
recommendations, or decisions influencing real or virtual environments;

 (2) uses machine and human–based inputs to perceive real and virtual
environments and abstracts those perceptions into models through analysis in an
automated manner; and

 (3) uses model inference to formulate options for information or action.

 SECTION 2. AND BE IT FURTHER ENACTED, That:

 (a) There is a 3–1–1 Technical Advisory Committee.

 (b) The Committee consists of the following members:

 (1) one representative of a county that operates an existing 3–1–1 system,
designated by the Executive Director of the Maryland Association of Counties;

 (2) one representative of a county that does not operate a 3–1–1 system,
designated by the Executive Director of the Maryland Association of Counties;

 (3) one 9–1–1 Public Safety Answering Point Director, designated by the
Secretary of Emergency Management, with technical expertise from a county that operates
an existing 3–1–1 system, or their designee;

 (4) one 9–1–1 Public Safety Answering Point Director, designated by the
Secretary of Emergency Management, with technical expertise from a county that does not
operate a 3–1–1 system, or their designee;
